chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza and Hisham and Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That some women entered upon him, and a woman from them asked him about Al-Sahq (lesbianism), so he said: 'Its penalty is the penalty of the adulterer.'
The woman said, 'Has Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that in the Quran?' He said, 'Yes.' She said, 'And where is it?' He said, 'They are the dwellers of Al-Rass.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الرَّسِّ: The dwellers of Al-Rass (a term from Surah Al-Furqan)

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the penalty of lesbianism in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) established that the hadd penalty for lesbianism (Al-Sahq) is equivalent to that of the adulterer, a ruling derived from the Quranic description of 'the dwellers of the Well' (Al-Rass). While the specific term for lesbianism is not explicitly named in the text, Shia scholars interpret this phrase as a metaphorical reference to the practice, linking it to the story of Lot's people. This narration highlights the method of deriving legal rulings through contextual interpretation of Quranic verses by the Imams.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza and Hisham and hafs,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, some women having come over to him, so a woman from them asked himasws about the lesbianism. So heasws said: ‘The Penalty (Hadd) is the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer’.

So the woman said, ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has not Mentioned that in the Quran?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’. She said, ‘And where is it?’ Heasws said: ‘These are [25:38] the dwellers of the Al-Rass’.
